s: Part (a): both processes in the green leaf
Part (b): only respiration in the roots

questions.q: A bean seed germinates in a dark cupboard and its shoot grows 3 cm in two days with no sunlight. Which source of the energy for this growth fits the chapter?
questions.a: Respiration of the stored food, using oxygen, releases the energy that is used for growth and development.
o: Respiration of stored food, using oxygen
Photosynthesis in the dark, using stored sunlight
Sunlight absorbed directly by the shoot in the cupboard
The carbon dioxide in the air around the shoot

questions.q:
Anita's group repeats Activity 10.8 in the dark for 24 hours with three flasks, each joined to its own tube of lime water. Flask 1 holds 20 g of soaked moong seeds on wet cotton, flask 2 holds wet cotton only, and flask 3 holds 5 g of fresh spinach leaves on wet cotton. The lime water of flask 1 turns milky and that of flask 2 stays clear. Rohit says flask 3 will stay clear 'because leaves release oxygen, not carbon dioxide'. Sneha says it will turn milky.
(a) What does flask 2 show?
(b) Whose prediction for flask 3 fits the chapter, and why?
(c) Flask 3 turns slightly milky, less than flask 1. Rohit now says 'so leaves respire less than seeds'. Does this set-up allow that conclusion?
(d) What would the group have to change to compare how fast seeds and leaves respire?
questions.a: (a) The wet cotton alone does not turn lime water milky, so the carbon dioxide in flask 1 comes from the seeds. (b) Sneha's: all parts of a plant, green or non-green, respire, so the leaves release carbon dioxide; in the dark they cannot photosynthesise, so no oxygen is being released by them. (c) No. The two flasks hold different kinds of plant part and different masses (20 g and 5 g), so a difference in milkiness could be due to the amount. The result shows only that leaves also release carbon dioxide. (d) Use equal masses of seeds and leaves, and equal time, with the same amount of lime water in each tube.
s: Part (a): cotton alone gives clear lime water, so seeds are the source
Part (b): Sneha, because all parts respire and the leaves are in the dark
Part (c): no, different parts and masses
Part (d): equal masses, time and lime water

questions.q:
(a) Name two changes of a growing plant, mentioned in Section 10.1, that need the energy released in respiration.
(b) Priya says: 'A plant in the dark cannot respire, since respiration needs sunlight.' Evaluate.
questions.a: (a) Any two: new leaves and branches emerging, increase in height, thickening of the stem. (b) Wrong: respiration does not need sunlight, and all parts of a plant respire. In the dark it is photosynthesis that stops.
s: Part (a): two growth changes
Part (b): respiration does not need sunlight; photosynthesis stops in the dark

questions.q: A student says the energy for a root to grow comes from photosynthesis in the root itself. Show that this cannot be so, and say what the root uses instead.
questions.a: A root is non-green and under the soil, so it has no chlorophyll and no sunlight, and photosynthesis cannot occur in it. Roots still respire, because all parts of a plant respire: they break down glucose, using oxygen, to release energy. The glucose is food made in the leaves.
s: Root has no chlorophyll or sunlight, so no photosynthesis
All parts respire, so the root breaks down glucose with oxygen
Glucose is made in the leaves

questions.q:
Look at the word equation of respiration: Glucose + Oxygen gives Carbon dioxide + Water + Energy.
(a) Which substance on the left side is a gas taken from the air?
(b) A root needs glucose for this. Where is that glucose made, and which tubes bring it?
questions.a: (a) Oxygen. (b) It is made in the leaves by photosynthesis and brought to the root through the phloem.
s: Part (a): oxygen
Part (b): made in the leaves, carried by the phloem

questions.q:
Match each item with the statement that goes with it.
Match Column I with Column II.
1. Lime water turning milky in Activity 10.8
2. A green leaf in bright sunlight
3. A root under the soil
4. The energy released in respiration

a. Both photosynthesis and respiration occur
b. Respiration occurs but photosynthesis cannot
c. More carbon dioxide than in normal air
d. Used for growth and development
questions.a: Milky lime water shows extra carbon dioxide; a sunlit green leaf does both processes; a root respires but cannot photosynthesise; the energy is used for growth.

questions.q:
In a school lab in Coimbatore, two flasks are kept in the dark for 24 hours. Flask 1 holds soaked chana seeds on wet cotton. Flask 2 holds an equal amount of wet cotton only. Each is joined by a tube to its own test tube of lime water. Next morning the lime water in one tube is milky and in the other it is clear, but the students forgot to note which tube went with which flask. A student says, 'The wet cotton must have made the lime water milky.'
(a) Which flask must have been joined to the milky tube, and why?
(b) Name the gas, and what produced it.
(c) What is the purpose of flask 2?
(d) Judge the student's statement, using the fact that both flasks hold the same wet cotton.
questions.a: (a) Flask 1, the one with the seeds, because only the seeds respire and release gas. (b) Carbon dioxide, produced by the seeds as they respire. (c) Flask 2 shows the effect of the wet cotton alone, to compare with the flask with seeds. (d) The statement is wrong: both flasks hold the same wet cotton, yet only one lime water turned milky, so the cotton cannot be the cause; the seeds' respiration is.
s: Part (a): flask 1, as the seeds respire
Part (b): carbon dioxide from respiring seeds
Part (c): flask 2 is the comparison
Part (d): same cotton but only one milky tube, so cotton is not the cause

questions.q: Tina says: 'Respiration releases the energy a plant needs, so a plant that is respiring in the dark will keep making glucose from that energy.' Do you agree?
questions.a: Partly right. It is correct that respiration releases the energy the plant uses for growth and development. It is wrong that respiration makes glucose: respiration breaks glucose down, using oxygen, while glucose is made by photosynthesis, which needs sunlight and chlorophyll and so stops in the dark.
s: Verdict: partly right
Right part: respiration releases energy used for growth
Wrong part: respiration breaks glucose down; photosynthesis makes it and needs sunlight

questions.q:
Statement 1: A plant kept in the dark for two days still respires in all its parts.
Statement 2: In respiration the glucose made by photosynthesis is broken down, using oxygen, to release energy.
Statement 3: The extra carbon dioxide that turns the lime water milky in Activity 10.8 is released by the seeds themselves.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.a: All three are correct.
o: 1, 2 and 3
1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
